name: One Hyde Park — Apartment B.07.1 Level 07 — evidence-based draft

scale.basis: Approximately 4.0 cm per source pixel, estimated from a 22–23 pixel ordinary Bedroom 4 ensuite doorway assumed near 90 cm; all positions use translation (250,80) source pixels. No legible linear dimension is provided.

assumptions: The source raster is 1086 x 1536 pixels. Geometry was traced in source pixels, x rightward and y downward; one transform is used throughout: cm = 4.0 * (pixel - (250,80)).

Scale is estimated: the ordinary ensuite doorway on the north edge of Bedroom 4 bathroom near source (437,839) spans about 22-23 pixels; a nominal 90 cm opening gives approximately 4 cm/pixel. The printed @A3 ratio is not treated as raster calibration. Actual luxury-apartment doors may be wider, so absolute dimensions remain uncertain.
Source states Level 07. This draft contains only that single apartment floor, level 7; floor height is an editable 280 cm assumption.

Windows use floor-to-ceiling fixed glass as a semantic-white-model presentation default. The source does not establish sill, glazing height, or glass type. Door style and heights are editable ordinary defaults.

Exterior glazing bands are grouped into large openings between visible solid piers; fine mullions are not separate walls. Balcony access at north and south is ambiguous and represented by one ordinary central door flanked by glass.

Balcony decks, railings and dashed outer balcony limits, the external shared stairs/lifts, access arrows, labels, rugs, planting and drawing ornament are omitted rather than interpreted as apartment walls.

The bowed entrance-hall right boundary is represented by a quadratic curve. Diagonal guest-bedroom and bathroom partitions are preserved. Small shower-screen lines are generally represented by shower fixture footprints rather than room partitions.

Detached reception divider strips and AV / kitchen / dressing storage are interpreted as semantic cabinet or unknown blocks; precise full-height-versus-low-divider classification needs user review. The AV perimeter is tentatively retained as a full-height enclosure.
Tiny utility rectangles with crossing diagonals are uncertain and categorized as unknown blocks; their use and dimensions require review. The service core is not reconstructed.

Furniture and fixtures are independently editable rectangular occupancy blocks. Curved tubs, piano and rounded tables are bounding rectangles. Width/depth and positions are traced or estimated from their visible footprint; all heights and styles are assumptions.

Dense service and ensuite door swings, principal-bath dressing access and internal prep-kitchen access are partly ambiguous at this raster resolution and carry reduced confidence. No invisible room or partition has been added to fill blank areas.
